name: Tiger Pest Control
subject: 🐯 Your testimonials section has no testimonials in it
body:
Hi team,

Your What Our Customers Are Saying section has no customers saying anything. It is an empty heading. And every social icon on the site links to the front page of Facebook, Instagram, or TikTok instead of to a real Tiger Pest profile, while the service photos look like stock images rather than your own technicians.

For a Duluth pest control company with a Georgia Certified Operator behind it, that missing proof is the whole sale. People choose the company whose reviews they can actually read.

I build websites for home service companies, and I would rebuild yours around real trust signals: genuine testimonials, your own photos, clear pages for the services you sell. Pest control work I have done includes Eco La Termite (ecolatermite.com) and Find Pest Pros (orkin.findpestpros.com), a pest control directory built to match homeowners with local operators.

Happy to mock up the new homepage first, free, so you can see exactly what would change.

Want me to draft it?

Thanks for your time,
Hassan

name: New South Overhead Garage Doors
subject: 🚪 Your whole website is a single short page
body:
Hi team,

Your entire web presence is one short page: four brief service blurbs and a stock photo credited to Wikimedia Commons. No reviews, no photos of your own installs, no address, nothing that tells a Savannah homeowner why your crew should get the call over the next company on the list.

Garage door work is an emergency purchase half the time. Someone with a broken spring is on their phone, comparing two or three companies within minutes, and the thin page loses that comparison almost every time.

I build websites for home service companies, and a proper site for you does not need to be huge, just convincing: services, real photos, reviews, and a quote form that works. You can see the style in Total Plumbing (totalplumbing.net), a home service site that is clean and fast for phone searches, and Leal Roofing (leal-roofing.com), built around quick calls and quotes.

I will mock up a homepage for New South first, free, so you can judge it before spending a cent.

Shall I?

Thanks for your time,
Hassan

name: Ampt Electric
subject: ⚡ Your reviews are showing as raw code on your homepage
body:
Hi team,

Quick thing I spotted on the Ampt homepage: under Popular Electric Services, where your Google reviews should appear, the page prints a line of raw code, [trustindex no-registration=google], as plain text. The review widget is broken, so the social proof block shows code instead of stars. Your email address is also buried in small print at the very bottom of the page.

For a licensed Kennesaw electrician and a Nextdoor Neighborhood Fave, those reviews are your best salesman, and right now they are invisible.

I build websites for home service companies, and fixing this properly means a homepage where reviews actually load, services are easy to scan, and contacting you takes one tap. Electrical sites I have done include DP Electric, a clean site for a local electrician, and Electrician Squad (electriciansquad.com), built around fast quote requests.

I can mock up a corrected homepage first, free, and you can see the difference side by side.

Want me to put it together?

Thanks for your time,
Hassan

name: Cool Max, Inc.
subject: ❄️ Your site still runs on http and a dated template
body:
Hi team,

Cool Max clearly has the licenses and the track record, but the website has not kept up with the company. It is an old vendor template still running on http instead of https, with generic stock photos, including a default financing image, and a layout that feels a decade old. Browsers also flag http sites as not secure, which is a bad first impression for a Johns Creek homeowner about to hand over their address and phone number.

A modern site for an established HVAC company does not need gimmicks. It needs secure pages, your real services up front, and a phone number that is impossible to miss.

That is the kind of work I do for home service companies. Two HVAC sites I built: Parker and Sons (parkerandsons.com), a large clean site that still loads fast, and Emergency HVAC Squad (emergencyhvacsquad.com), built for people who need help the same day.

I can mock up a refreshed homepage for Cool Max first, free of charge, before you decide on anything bigger.

Open to seeing it?

Thanks for your time,
Hassan
